verdict.reasoning: Patient reports, “this really horrible pain on the left side of my head… I kind of woke up this morning… Is the headache still present now? – Yes, it is.”

Headache description and timing: “left side of my head… a real kind of headache feeling” and “Probably around 5:30ish” when it woke him; this reasonably implies a left-sided (left/front) headache starting at 5:30 AM.
Patient: “I’ve had a bit of a history with headaches but nothing as severe as this before… this time it’s just kind of more prominent on the left side.”
Doctor asks about bright lights; patient: “I’m a little bit sensitive. It kind of makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can’t really handle,” which is mild photophobia.
Doctor: “Do you have any neck stiffness at all?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor: “do you have any fever?” Patient: “No.”
Patient: “Are you feeling nauseous at all? – Not really. Like when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy… but… seems to be fine.” This indicates no significant current nausea.
Patient: “when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy, but that’s kind of… now and I seems to be fine,” indicating transient dizziness that resolved.

Patient: “When I lay down, like, it kind of feels a little bit sore at first and it takes me a while to get comfortable… but then again, that just kind of soothes a little bit… I would say [ultimately it’s better when you lie down].”
Doctor: “have you taken anything for it yet?” Patient: “I’ve taken some paracetamol… Has that helped? – Not really, no.”

Transcript only notes pain is initially more sore when first lying down and then improves; there is no mention of headache being worse with general activity or ‘initial lying down phases’ versus ‘after onset’ beyond what is already described.

Doctor: “You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like, but the ibuprofen is actually more effective for migraine,” consistent with continuation as needed.
